clue.text: Swamp with antelope eating tons

indicators.note: the antelope swallows the next piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A marsh where an antelope is busy devouring a great quantity of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts T inside ELAND after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swamp is a waterlogged tract of ground, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Seaweed beginning to wither on frame

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken from wither

parts.note: a rack is a framework for holding or stretching things

explanation.surface: Seaweed starting to shrivel while it hangs on a drying frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrack is coarse brown seaweed cast up on the shore, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: After working on yacht, in principle it goes very fast

definitions.text: in principle it goes very fast

indicators.note: the following word on is placed after the rearranged letters rather than before them
fodder that is working is being worked over, so the letters of yacht are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that, once you get the yacht going, theoretically races along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in principle' belongs to the definition: the particle exists only in theory, never observed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachyon is a theoretical particle that would always travel faster than light, existing only in theory.

clue.text: Crown close cousin with kiss

parts.note: apes are our nearest relatives in evolution, humanity's close cousins
X is written for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A relative greeted at a coronation, perhaps, with a crown and a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of something is its top or peak, the same as its highest point.

clue.text: Extortionate price foolish brother gayly bid

indicators.note: a foolish arrangement is a silly, disordered one, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A daft sibling cheerfully makes a ridiculously high offer at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolish' rearranges the letters of BROTHER GAYLY BID; GAYLY is the less common spelling of gaily, chosen for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight robbery is an idiom for charging blatantly too much, open theft in broad day.

clue.text: Some tablets, another and then another to get back into shape

indicators.note: getting back means going in the opposite direction, so the assembled letters are read from the end

parts.note: Es are ecstasy tablets, written as plural E
a pill is another kind of tablet
E, a single ecstasy tablet, is yet another

explanation.surface: Someone recovering their figure by taking one tablet after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get back' reverses ES PILL E. E for an ecstasy tablet is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is an oval, a particular geometric figure, so it is one kind of shape.

clue.text: Getting level grade for paper

parts.note: evening something out is making it level
a standard is a grade or level of quality

explanation.surface: Achieving an equal mark on an exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Evening Standard is a London newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Evening Standard is a London daily newspaper, an example of a paper.

clue.text: Book on Leonardo reissued

indicators.note: a reissued edition comes out again in new form, so these letters are put out in a new order

explanation.surface: A volume about Leonardo da Vinci has been republished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reissued' rearranges ON LEONARDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna Doone is R. D. Blackmore's 1869 romance novel, an example of a book.

clue.text: Unable to move, university housed one in flat

indicators.note: the combined piece is set inside the word for the flat

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat or home

indicators.note: the university gives lodging to the next piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A student stuck in their flat, provided by the university.
explanation.walkthrough: The London School of Economics is a college of the University of London, so it can stand for 'university'.
explanation.definitionFit: Palsied means affected by palsy, paralysed and so incapable of motion.

clue.text: Old ascetic conceals cold heart

indicators.note: the ascetic hides the next piece within him, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Essenes were an ancient Jewish ascetic sect
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An ancient hermit hides a frosty, unfeeling heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' puts C inside ESSENE, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of a matter is its core or essential nature, its innermost substance.

clue.text: Perfect example of first car …

parts.note: arch- means chief or first, as in archbishop
the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A catalogue entry for the finest specimen of the earliest motor car.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue, which says 'another' car.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original model or typical specimen of which others are copies.

clue.text: … another goes smoothly along

definitions.meaning: to travel on wheels or move evenly forward

explanation.surface: Continuing the motoring theme: a second vehicle glides past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' only makes sense with the ellipsis: it means another car, the Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls is the short name for a Rolls-Royce, the luxury car, and also a verb for moving on wheels.

clue.text: Floor is fine for cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends a letter round from one end to the other, here the first to the back

parts.note: something that is okay is fine or acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone saying a floor is fine to ride a bike on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cycling' moves the O of OKAY to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to knock them out, which boxers abbreviate KO and spell out as kayo.

clue.text: With people, share prediction

parts.note: divi is informal for a dividend, one's share of profits
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A forecaster sharing a prophecy with the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Divination is foretelling the future by supernatural means, a form of forecasting.

clue.text: Band consuming drinks in cabaret performance

indicators.note: the band takes in the drinks, so they go inside it

parts.note: a stripe is a band of colour
teas are drinks

explanation.surface: A group of musicians downing drinks during a nightclub show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, which fits the cabaret surface, but here it means a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is an erotic act of undressing performed as entertainment in clubs.

clue.text: Inform of allergic reaction to tin?

indicators.note: the reaction is attached to the tin, placed on after it

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
an itch is a common allergic reaction

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone itches when touching tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To snitch is slang for informing on someone, telling tales to authority.

clue.text: Late king finally coming out for princess, a northerner

indicators.note: the closing consonant of the king's name leaves and another piece takes its place

parts.note: George VI was the late king, or any dead King George
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A dead monarch's name finally replaced by a princess's, for a man from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the later of the king's two Gs goes, hence 'finally'. A Geordie is someone from Tyneside, around Newcastle in northeast England.
explanation.definitionFit: Geordie is the nickname for a native of Newcastle upon Tyne, in the north of England.

clue.text: One opening homeless person's file

indicators.note: the numeral breaks open the next word and sits inside it

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for a homeless person who sleeps rough
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone opening a rough sleeper's case file.
explanation.walkthrough: A dosser is British slang for someone sleeping rough.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of documents about a person or subject, a type of file.

clue.text: Injured old man calls wizard in

indicators.note: with calls, the old man brings the wizard inside

parts.note: one's old man is informal for one's father, dad
a mage is a magician or wizard

explanation.surface: A hurt elderly man summons a magician to heal him.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion signal is split: 'calls' and 'in' together, as in calling a doctor in.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged means harmed or hurt, an adjective matching injured.

clue.text: Given call to attention, ignored

definitions.meaning: 'shun is the drill command shortened from attention

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to stand to attention, then ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: ''Shun!' is the barked military short form of 'Attention!', so the first definition reads the word as that command plus -ed.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun someone is to avoid or ostracise them deliberately, so being shunned is being ignored.

clue.text: Soldier's gear, which stays at home

indicators.note: to stay is to prop or hold, so the word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns
in means at home

explanation.surface: A piece of military kit that never leaves the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays at home' reads as one phrase, but 'stays' means props up or holds, the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin hat is a steel helmet worn by soldiers, part of their kit.

clue.text: Imogen gets to open some bananas, not initially for flavouring

indicators.note: the phrase breaks open the next piece and sits inside it
without its opening letter the word for the bananas loses its first letter

parts.note: a hand is a bunch of bananas
the setter is Imogen, so the setter's name stands for I
to see a point is to get it, understand it

explanation.surface: The setter cutting into a bunch of bananas to flavour a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand is the cluster of bananas growing on one stalk; dropping its first letter leaves AND, which 'to open' splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the seed of anise, used as a liquorice-tasting flavouring in sweets and drinks.

clue.text: Charlatan, one eluding policeman at store

indicators.note: the numeral escapes from the policeman, so it is removed

parts.note: a Mountie is a Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer
I is the Roman numeral for one
a bank is a store, as in a blood bank

explanation.surface: A con man evading a police officer at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eluding' takes I out of MOUNTIE, leaving MOUNTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountebank is a swindler or quack, originally a seller of fake medicines from a platform.

clue.text: Tree minute but unbending

parts.note: the fir is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A tiny tree that will not bow in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' reads as tiny but is the time unit, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means resolute and not yielding, a straight synonym for inflexible.

clue.text: One half-day, plus a day

parts.note: half of the word Monday is its first three letters

explanation.surface: A working half-day followed by another full day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-day' takes half the letters of MONDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A monad is a single indivisible unit, from the Greek for unity.

clue.text: Refuse to have gospel read out

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so the gospel's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Mark is one of the four gospels

explanation.surface: Declining to have a passage of scripture read in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun: waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the residue of skins and pips left after pressing grapes, waste matter.

clue.text: Commonly about to hear one who's had it

indicators.note: hearing signals that the word for the doomed one is spoken, not written

parts.note: a goner is someone doomed or done for

explanation.surface: Listening to a dying person's slangy last words.
explanation.walkthrough: The match works in non-rhotic British speech, where the final R is not sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonna is the colloquial contraction of going to, meaning about to.

clue.text: In battle with airline I get in the final word

parts.note: El Al is the Israeli national airline

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word

explanation.surface: Someone in a fight with an airline insists on having the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get in' puts I inside AMEN, before N.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein was the 1942 North African battle where Allied forces defeated Rommel's army.

clue.text: Shambling comedian's hesitation ending in mockery

parts.note: Ken Dodd was a Liverpool comedian
er is the sound of hesitating

indicators.note: the closing letter of mockery is taken

explanation.surface: A stumbling comic pauses, his act ending in ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a famous British comedian from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery describes someone unsteady or tottering from age, moving in a shuffling way.

clue.text: Chose to be made redundant as detective?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., removed from the CID, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: A detective deciding to take redundancy.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police; the prefix de- means removed from.
explanation.definitionFit: To have decided is to have made a choice, the past tense matching chose.
